posts.title: 85th anniversary of the U.S. rejecting a Japanese settlement offer; what would have happened if we’d never fought in the Pacific?
posts.description: On November 20, 1941, the Japanese proposed an agreement with the United States in which both countries would agree to leave Southern Indochina and the South Pacific alone. President Roosevelt would unfreeze Japanese assets and un-embargo oil sales to Japan (i.e., Japan would become a huge customer for U.S. oil and other raw materials).
